title: Crystallographic Analysis of Trapiche Ruby using Low-Vacuum Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy, Electron Backscatter Diffraction Pattern, Raman Spectroscopy, and Field Emission Electron Probe Microscopy
content: Trapiche ruby is a ruby showing textures with six arms and six growth sectors. It has been attracting among jewelry field because of its unique appearance after the early works about it [1-3]. Sunagawa et al. reported important scientific work on it. They showed elemental mapping and optical micrographs, and they also discussed the crystal growth mechanism of trapiche ruby [4]. Recently, we reported elemental and crystallographic study of trapiche ruby using modern updated instruments such as micro X-ray fluorescence spectroscope, low vacuum type field emission scanning electron microscope and high reciprocal space resolution X-ray diffraction [5]. Our main result, especially the elemental analysis, had good agreement with the study of Sunagawa and colleagues, but there were still uncertainties about the crystal growth mechanism of trapiche ruby. In this study, we carried out experimental analysis using low-vacuum scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), electron backscatter diffraction pattern (EBSD), Raman spectroscopy, and field emission electron probe microscopy (EPMA) to elucidate the microscopic structure, because it may be useful for future discussion about the crystal growth of trapiche ruby.
